title: Autotune defaults for batching/caching, add quantization profiles, and expose unit-econ tooling
author: Liam Chen
description: Context: This PR implements autotuning defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduces a validated set of quantization profiles for common model families, and surfaces unit-economics (uecon) tooling in the console and CLI. Motivation: reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs and make it straightforward for teams to adopt cost-saving defaults. Summary of changes: 1) Runtime: add new default batching policy 'adaptive_latency_sensitive' with dynamic windowing and priority inversion protection; add cache TTL heuristics and adaptive prefix-KV cache eviction to improve effective cache hit ratio under bursty workloads. 2) Quantization: add qprofile-nf4, qprofile-int8-fast, and qprofile-int8-balanced with validation harness and runtime fallback rules. 3) Tooling: expose /admin/uecon endpoint, add CLI command 'redwood uecon analyze' to compute per-route unit economics, and add dashboard widgets to the Console for per-model and per-route UEcon breakdowns. 4) Config/migrations: extend cluster policy schema with cost.autotune.v1 entries and add migration script to migrate existing policy defaults. 5) Observability: add metrics batch_size, effective_cache_hit_ratio, quant_mode tag, and unit_econ_cost_per_token metric. Tests and rollout: unit tests, integration e2e against perf-canary workloads, and a staged rollout behind feature-flag 'cost.autotune.v1' with canary routing. All CI checks passed. Rollout notes: staged canary to 5% of traffic for 48h before ramp. Checklist: - [x] runtime changes implemented - [x] quant profiles validated against evaluation harness - [x] Console + CLI surfaces implemented - [x] docs and release notes updated - [x] migration script included Related work: ENG-4123 and ENG-4189. Backward compatibility: runtime will automatically fall back to float32 variants if a quant profile fails validation or an unsupported hardware path is selected. See commits, changed files, and review comments for details.

review_comments: Priya Patel: The adaptive policy looks good overall. Can you add a guard for long-running requests so they do not get starved when batching increases? Also prefer feature-flag gating for any config schema changes.
Liam Chen (author): Added max_batch_latency cap and gated schema migration behind 'cost.autotune.v1'. See commit b2d1f4a and e1b3c22.
Carlos Mendes: How does quant fallback interact with Dedicated GPU pools that do not support INT8 on older drivers? Please ensure we have a safe fallback and signal in metrics.

Liam Chen (author): Quant profiles include hardware capability checks; if driver/hw unsupported, engine falls back to float32 and emits quant_mode='fallback' metric. Added validation harness tests and an integration test that simulates older drivers.
Evan Brooks: Verified perf-canary against a 50k request sample; effective_cache_hit_ratio improved by ~22% and median p99 latency remained within SLO. LGTM.
Priya Patel: Approving after confirming migration script and docs. Approved.

release_notes: Added adaptive batching default 'adaptive_latency_sensitive' and KV-prefix cache TTL heuristics to reduce per-token cost. Introduced three validated quantization profiles (qprofile-nf4, qprofile-int8-fast, qprofile-int8-balanced) with runtime fallback to float32. Exposed unit-economics tooling: Console dashboard widgets and 'redwood uecon analyze' CLI command. Migration script included. Feature gated under cost.autotune.v1.
